info.name: Store Management API — Full Test Run
info.description:
Run these top to bottom (Runner, or one by one). IDs created early are saved into collection variables and reused later, and the last folder deletes everything it created so the run is repeatable.

Set {{baseUrl}} in the Variables tab if your port is not 3000.

item.name: 0 — Health & discovery
item.description: Prove the API is up and talking to PostgreSQL before testing anything else.

request.description: Pings the database. If this says "connected", Express AND Postgres are both fine.
Lists every available endpoint. Useful as a reminder of the URL shapes.

item.name: 1 — Categories
item.description: Simplest resource: full CRUD, uniqueness, validation, and the delete guard.

request.description: Should show the 4 seeded categories with a meta block.

exec: pm.test("returns the created row with an id", () => pm.expect(d.id).to.be.a("number"));

request.description: Saves the new id into {{categoryId}} for every later request.
The unique index on categories.name fires; Sequelize throws UniqueConstraintError and errorHandler maps it to 409.
Blocked by express-validator BEFORE the controller runs. Note the details array naming the field.
Includes the products belonging to this category (empty for now).
The id param is validated as a positive integer, so this never reaches the database.
Partial update — send only what changes.
Case-insensitive partial match (ILIKE) on the name.

item.name: 2 — Suppliers
item.description: Same CRUD shape, plus email format and email uniqueness.

request.description: The stray "id" in the body is ignored — the controller whitelists writable fields.

item.name: 3 — Products
item.description: The core resource: relations, computed fields, filtering, and the quantity guard.

request.description: Watch two things: the SKU comes back uppercase, and an opening IN movement is written to the ledger.
The controller checks the relation exists and returns a readable 400 instead of a raw foreign-key error.
Includes category, supplier, and the last 10 stock movements.
Searches name, SKU and description at once.
sortBy is whitelisted, so it cannot be used to inject SQL into ORDER BY.
Stops a client asking for the whole table in one request.

exec: pm.test("every row really is low", () => pm.response.json().data.forEach(p => pm.expect(p.quantity).to.be.at.most(p.reorderLevel)));

request.description: quantity <= reorderLevel, compared column-to-column in SQL. The seeded water and milk should appear.
Deliberately blocked. Stock may only change through /stock so every movement is recorded.

item.name: 4 — Stock movements
item.description: The audited ledger. Every quantity change is a transaction plus a history row.

request.description: Opening 40 + 25 = 65. The movement records before and after.
Rolled back inside the transaction — stock stays at 60 and no ledger row is written.
An adjustment always needs a written justification.
Absolute set, not a delta. The ledger stores the size of the correction (10).
Four rows: opening IN 40, IN 25, OUT 5, ADJUSTMENT 10. Newest first.

item.name: 5 — Integrity checks & cleanup
item.description: Proves the delete guards work, then removes everything this run created so you can run it again.

request.description: Refused because a product still points at it. Prevents orphaned data.
204 means success with no body. Its stock movements cascade away with it.
